Details of the proof are in, e.g., Hoffman (2001). Hence, if is decreased by a factor 2, then has to decrease by a factor of 4 (a factor of 2 is not enough!). This requires only operations instead of as with Gaussian elimination, since one can use the fact that there are a lot of zeros in the matrix. We won't discuss the algorithm.
